newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk declines to endorse Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk declines to endorse Hun Sen.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk indicated on Sunday that he would not endorse Cambodia's new government, but stopped short of accusing the country's powerful second prime minister of staging a coup.

The king, who is currently in Beijing receiving medical treatment, called on Second Prime Minister Hun Sen to respect the constitution and all laws and international agreements signed by the government since the 1991 peace treaty.

In his first public statement since his son, First Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was ousted, Sihanouk said he was not willing to sign royal decrees and other documents covering the make-up of Hun Sen's "victorious" government.

"I will tell Hun Sen...that it is up to Chea Sim, acting chief of state, to sign the (documents). I will not be opposed to his signature. But I will not personally sign," Sihanouk said in an interview with staff from his information bulletin.
A copy of the interview was released by the palace in Phnom Penh on Sunday.
Ranariddh was ousted on July 6 after two days of battles in Phnom Penh between forces loyal to him and those under Hun Sen.
Sihanouk declined to pass judgement when asked if Hun Sen had staged a coup.
"I cannot place myself in 'judgement' with regard to this 'coup' or 'non-coup d'etat' in Phnom Penh and the rest of Cambodia," he said.

Sihanouk also said he fully supported a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning the recent fighting between troops loyal to the two premiers and urging all parties to solve their differences peacefully.

He said he hoped international donors, a number of whom have frozen aid to Cambodia, would continue to give direct humanitarian assistance to victims of the fighting, hospitals and prisoners, and would work to improve poor prison conditions.
Sihanouk himself was ousted as head of state in a republican coup in 1970. He was restored as monarch in 1993 after U.N.-organised elections.
The elections were won by Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party but resulted in a power-sharing arrangement with Hun Sen.
